headline: SILVER MINE RISES: Sunshine Silver Raises $270M in NYSE IPO to Restart Idaho's Storied Silver Valley Operation
snippet: Sunshine Silver Mining & Refining (NYSE: SSMR) began trading Thursday after pricing its IPO at $13.50/share, raising $270M from 20 million shares. The company plans to restart the historic Sunshine Mine in Idaho's Silver Valley, once one of North America's largest silver producers, as silver trades near $74/oz.

headline: MONSTER HIT: DPM Metals Drills 713 Metres at 2.52 g/t AuEq in New Porphyry Discovery Adjacent to Bulgaria's Chelopech Mine
snippet: DPM Metals (ASX: DPM) announced a world-class porphyry discovery at its Brevene licence in Bulgaria, returning 713 metres at 2.52 g/t gold equivalent — comprising 1.31 g/t Au and 1.16% Cu — contiguous with the producing Chelopech mine. Five drill rigs are now working the target with 15,000 metres planned through year-end; this is DPM's fourth significant discovery since 2023.

headline: GOLD DETHRONES DOLLAR: ECB Confirms Gold Has Overtaken US Treasuries as World's Top Global Reserve Asset
snippet: The ECB's annual financial stability report shows gold's share of global central bank reserves climbed to 27% by end-2025, surpassing US Treasuries (22%) for the first time on record. ECB President Christine Lagarde attributed the shift to geopolitical tensions and the weaponisation of dollar reserves following Russia sanctions — a structural change with long-term implications for gold demand.

headline: GOLD DROPS TO $4,440: Strong US Jobs Data Revives Fed Rate Fears, Sends Precious Metals to Two-Week Lows
snippet: Gold fell to $4,440/oz Wednesday while silver dropped to ~$74/oz, approaching two-week lows, as stronger-than-expected US labor market data reinforced expectations that the Fed will hold rates elevated longer. The ongoing US-Iran military standoff near the Strait of Hormuz adds an inflationary energy shock that paradoxically pressures both metals through rate-expectations channels.

headline: COPPER SUPPLY CRISIS: Goldman Eyes $13,735, Citi Calls $15,000/t as Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula Output Collapses
snippet: Goldman Sachs raised its end-2026 copper target to $13,735/tonne after cutting global mine supply forecasts by 350,000 tonnes, citing Freeport's Grasberg underground flood and Kamoa-Kakula seismic disruptions — neither expected at full capacity before 2028. Citigroup is more aggressive, projecting $14,500/t this month and $15,000 within a year, with the ex-US supply deficit now forecast at 640,000 tonnes.

headline: NUCLEAR FUEL PUSH: Urenco USA Plans 50% Uranium Enrichment Expansion in $4B+ Build at New Mexico Facility
snippet: Urenco USA announced a multi-billion-dollar expansion of the US's only commercial uranium enrichment facility in Eunice, New Mexico, adding 2.1 million SWU of new capacity and lifting total output above 7 million SWU. Construction begins in 2029 with first production from new cascades in 2032, a direct response to US Section 232 policy designating uranium a national security asset.

headline: WATCH THE FED: Analyst Says June FOMC Meeting Is the Critical Pivot Point for Gold and Silver Direction
snippet: Asia-Pacific precious metals commentary argues the June 17 FOMC meeting is the key inflection point for metals direction: price weakness before the meeting likely represents a buying opportunity within the medium-term bull trend, while a sustained fall after the Fed decision could trigger institutional exits from long positions in gold and silver.

headline: INFLATION FIGHTS BACK: Why the Fed May Be Losing the Battle — and What It Means for Gold
snippet: Money Metals analyst examines the structural contradiction in Fed rate policy: tightening to fight service-sector and energy-driven inflation while the federal balance sheet continues expanding. Drawing parallels to the 1970s, the piece argues both inflation persistence and a future policy reversal support gold's dual role as a hedge — directly relevant context for junior mining investors watching the gold floor.

headline: TECK SELLS, MARUBENI BUYS: Valhalla Metals Closes Smucker VMS Copper-Zinc Deal in Alaska's Ambler District
snippet: Valhalla Metals (TSXV: VMXX) closed its acquisition of the Smucker copper-gold-silver-zinc VMS project from Teck American in Alaska's Ambler Mining District, completing a C$15M over-subscribed private placement with Teck (now 31.4% shareholder) and Marubeni as strategic co-investors. The deal doubles Valhalla's exposure to high-grade VMS deposits in one of North America's most prospective polymetallic belts.

headline: ROAD TO GOLD: Cambria Gold Breaks Ground on 23km Mine Access Road to High-Grade Red Mountain Deposit in BC
snippet: Cambria Gold Mines (TSXV: CAMB) has commenced construction on a 23km access road to its high-grade Red Mountain gold-silver deposit northeast of Stewart, BC, backed by Nisga'a Nation support. Phase I targets 13km to the base of Red Mountain by end-2026, enabling ore trucking to Cambria's existing 2,500 tpd Premier mill for processing.
